Three empty office blocks will become 420 rental homes

The city council approved on Tuesday a plan to convert three empty office buildings into 420 rental homes, the largest conversion of its kind in the region so far.

Under the plan, a third of the flats will be offered below market rates for at least twenty years. The council expects the first tenants to move in by the end of next year.

Developers have argued for months that the rules for changing a building's use were too slow. The new ordinance cuts the approval process from eighteen months to six.

Tenant groups welcomed the decision but warned that conversions alone will not bring rents down. They asked for a public register of empty homes and stronger inspections.

Economists consulted by this newspaper said the measure could add up to 2,000 homes over five years if other owners follow, a small but meaningful share of the yearly shortfall.
